lead: Glendale plumbing deals with hard water, desert heat and a mix of older slab homes and newer north-side tracts. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Glendale.
risk: hard water scale, slab leaks and aging pipes in older south Glendale homes
risk_short: hard water, slab leaks and old pipes
why: South Glendale and the Catlin Court area have homes from the 1940s to the 1970s, with galvanized supply lines and cast-iron or clay drains. North Glendale, around Arrowhead Ranch, was built mostly since the 1980s.
Homes sit on slabs, so leaks under the floor are common. Hard water and summer heat wear out water heaters.
water: Glendale's water comes from the Salt and Verde rivers, Colorado River water through the Central Arizona Project and groundwater. It is hard, so scale builds up in heaters and fixtures.
tips: Scope old clay sewer lines before buying.
Watch for warm spots on the floor.
areas: PipeMend works in Historic Downtown Glendale, Catlin Court, Arrowhead Ranch, Westgate, Bellair, Sierra Verde and every other Glendale neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Glendale Building Safety Division, and contractors need an Arizona Registrar of Contractors license.

faq.q: Is it Glendale, Arizona or Glendale, California?
faq.a: This page covers Glendale, Arizona, in the Phoenix area. PipeMend takes plumbing calls in both, and the phone line works anywhere in the U.S.
